subsystems.name: Regolith mining plant
subsystems.role: strips and hauls the silicate crust that supplies nearly all the mass.

subsystems.name: Solar furnace and refining
subsystems.role: uses concentrated sunlight to melt and split regolith into useful elements.

subsystems.name: Collector manufacturing
subsystems.role: turns refined material into thin photovoltaic film and structural frames.

subsystems.name: Electromagnetic launcher
subsystems.role: throws finished components off Mercury without rockets, using the planet's low gravity.

subsystems.name: Swarm elements
subsystems.role: the collectors themselves, orbiting the Sun as a coordinated fleet.

subsystems.name: Power delivery or use
subsystems.role: gets the collected energy to wherever it is wanted.

subsystems.name: Control network
subsystems.role: keeps millions of independent elements from shadowing or colliding.

buildSteps.title: Survey Mercury
buildSteps.detail: Map regolith chemistry, ice in permanently shadowed polar craters, and day–night temperature swings from about −180 °C to +430 °C.

buildSteps.title: Land robotic precursors
buildSteps.detail: Autonomous mining and refining machines land first; the planet has no atmosphere, so everything must be delivered and operated robotically.

buildSteps.title: Build surface power
buildSteps.detail: Concentrated solar thermal plants near the terminator work around Mercury's 88-day night; stored heat or chemical energy fills the gaps.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap materials production
buildSteps.detail: Regolith (roughly 20% silicon and 40% oxygen, with iron, magnesium and aluminium) is melted and electrolysed into silicon, metals and oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Expand manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: The plant builds copies of its own mining, refining and assembly equipment, so tonnage output grows without further launches from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Install the launchers
buildSteps.detail: Electromagnetic accelerators are built on the surface. Mercury's escape velocity of about 4.25 km/s is low enough to reach without rockets, and there is no air to slow the payload.

buildSteps.title: Launch and shape orbits
buildSteps.detail: Each component is released at a timed vector relative to Mercury's 47 km/s orbital motion, dropping it into a chosen heliocentric orbit; sunlight pressure on very thin films trims it further.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Elements are stacked into many inclined rings rather than one, so the collectors do not shade each other and the Sun is covered from every direction.

buildSteps.title: Deliver the energy
buildSteps.detail: Power is either used in place or beamed; diffraction spreads the beam over interplanetary distances, so transmission is the hardest unsolved engineering problem.

prerequisites.why: without exponential growth from local material, building the swarm's mass from Earth launches is impossible.

prerequisites.tech: In-situ resource utilisation on airless bodies
prerequisites.why: oxygen and metals have been extracted from lunar and asteroid simulants in laboratories, but never at industrial scale off Earth.
coilgun and railgun launchers have been demonstrated at small scale; nothing close to a kilometre-long orbital launcher exists.
microwave and laser power transmission has been shown in short-range experiments, not across interplanetary distances.

prerequisites.tech: Coordinated control of very large orbital fleets
prerequisites.why: millions of independent collectors in nested orbits require control that current space traffic systems cannot approach.
equipment near the Sun must survive intense ultraviolet, particle and thermal loads for decades.

pathway.milestone: laboratory refining of regolith into oxygen, metals and silicon; robotic mining concepts for the Moon and asteroids
pathway.unlocks: a first autonomous industrial foothold off Earth.

pathway.milestone: robotic mines and in-space manufacturing that build hardware from local material
pathway.unlocks: mass in orbit without paying Earth's launch cost.

pathway.milestone: a self-expanding industrial base on an airless body, with electromagnetic launch instead of rockets
pathway.unlocks: an exponential supply of collector mass — the concept in this tile.

pathway.milestone: a partial Dyson swarm capturing a meaningful fraction of the Sun's output
pathway.unlocks: a Kardashev Type II-scale energy supply and the option to beam power inward.

pathway.milestone: a full swarm enclosing the Sun
pathway.unlocks: energy limited only by the star, at the cost of dismantling Mercury and losing the inner Solar System's natural state.
